messages:
maya: Heads up — nightly perf run flagged ~35% p95/p99 regression on a subset of customer traces. Seems correlated with head_dim=30/unaligned heads; kernel picker is falling back to the generic SDPA slow path on SM86 when cache is warm. cc @oliver @tasha

oliver: Oof. Do we have a minimal repro? sequence lengths, batch sizes, kv-cache state?

maya: Quick notes from the run: small batches (bs=2), seqlen=64 for generation, kv-cache populated (prefix ~128). On SM86 machines the kernel selector chose flashv3-causal?fallback -> generic_sdpa. Profiler snippet:```
[kernel-select] model=MPT-7B head_dim=30 causal=true cache_hits=true
selected_kernel=generic_sdpa
expected=flash_attn_v3_causal
latency=12.3ms -> 16.5ms (per-token)
callsite=kv_cache_hit_path
```

sre-bot: incident-bot: perf-alert triggered: perf-regression:eng-runtime:2249999999 (alert-level: warning) :bell:

tasha: That pattern matches our headmod mismatch rule hitting heuristics. For head_dim not divisible by 8/16 we sometimes force fallback because tile shapes misalign on SM86. But I thought flashv3 had improved unaligned head handling. Could be interaction with causal prefetch + kv cache offsets.

kevin: I dug into kernel-table heuristics — we're using a strict tile-fit test that doesn't consider sequence-length distribution or kv-cache hot prefix. Proposed quick fix: add an architecture-aware relaxation for SM86 where head_dim % 8 != 0 but head_dim % 2 == 0 and seq<128 we allow the flashv3-causal path with a fallback guard. Patch snippet:```diff
- if (!tile_fits(model, arch)) select(generic_sdpa)
+ if (!tile_fits(model, arch) && !(arch==SM86 && head_dim%2==0 && seq<=128 && causal)) select(generic_sdpa)
```
This should reduce kernel switches for the customer traces.

oliver: Can you run a microbenchmark before merging? Need numbers on p50/p95/p99 and memory use. Also check SM80 where the old behavior might be preferable.

maya: Ran microbench on both archs, bs=1..4, seqlen sweep. Results (avg token latency ms):```
SM86 before: 12.1, 13.4, 16.9 (p50,p95,p99)
SM86 after-relax: 9.8, 11.0, 12.9
SM80 before: 9.6, 10.2, 11.5
SM80 after-relax: 9.9, 10.6, 11.9 (no significant regressions)
```
KV cache memory and correctness tests passed. No numerics drift on eval prompts.

tasha: Nice. We should also add a sequence-length histogram input to the autotuner so the picker uses the real workload distribution (prefetch can change effective seq). Put a hysteresis so frequent flips don't thrash.

kevin: Agreed. I'll open two PRs: one hotfix for the selector table (canary), and a follow-up to census the seqlen hist and add hysteresis. Canary config: 10% prod routing, metric to watch: kernel_switch_rate, p99_latency_per_route, error_rate.

oliver: Add a small safety timeout so if flash path faults we fallback immediately and record the stacktrace for kernel debugging. Also add an opt-in debug flag to log kernel pick reasons for 2 minutes.

maya: Will file the rollout ticket and tag @oncall-eng-runtime. PR will include microbench script and the profiler output. Rolling canary tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:

kevin: FYI, this also fixes one customer-reported spike from last week. I'll link the ticket in the PR.

oliver: Cool. After canary, let's run 24h synthetic with customer trace replay to ensure no late regressions.

maya: On it. Thanks all.
